正しさを、少し遅らせる

Why do some conversations turn negative even when you are only trying to be accurate? The issue may not be pessimism but timing: analysis arrives before emotional responsiveness. This essay connects negativity-bias research, Shelly Gable's active-constructive responding, Harvard research on follow-up questions, and Motivational Interviewing's righting reflex, then turns them into a practical rule: React → Ask → Analyze. The goal is not to become less accurate. It is to delay accuracy long enough to understand what kind of conversation is actually happening.
